# Cūḷabodhijātaka (Ja 443)
**ID:** Ja 443
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Cūḷabodhijātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja443
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cūḷabodhijātaka* (Ja 443, also spelled *Cullabodhijātaka*) belongs to the Dasanipāta of the Jātaka collection [Morris 1882]. According to the frame story, the Buddha recounted this birth tale while residing at Jetavana with reference to a passionate man [SuttaCentral]. In the narrative, the Bodhisatta renounces worldly life as the virtuous ascetic Cūḷabodhi and dwells in the royal park at Benares alongside his former wife, a brāhmaṇī of golden complexion who has likewise undertaken ascetic renunciation [Bareau; Hazra 1994; Morris 1882]. When the local king forcibly abducts the ascetic's former wife, she steadfastly rejects the king's advances, while Cūḷabodhi refuses to succumb to anger in order to safeguard his moral discipline (*sīla*); upon being questioned by the astonished king, the Bodhisatta delivers verses praising the eradication of anger [Anandajoti 2010; Hazra 1994; War Yar Mein Da 2015].
The episode forms a canonical narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka*, where Cūlabodhi's unyielding forbearance illustrates the perfection of moral virtue (*sīlapāramī*) [Bareau; Hazra 1994; Morris 1882]. SuttaCentral identifies resembling parallels in the *Siṅgāla Sutta* (DN 31) and the *Tatiyaagatisutta* (AN 4.19; cf. AN 4.17–18) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus documents Pali-internal text reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Catukkanipāta* of the Aṅguttara Nikāya (AN 4, sharing verses between §12.2–13.4 and AN 4.19) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the Pali tradition, the story is preserved as chapter 21 of Āryaśūra’s Sanskrit *Jātakamālā* (entitled *Cuddabodhi*, emended from manuscript readings of *Buddhabodhi*) and its Tibetan translation in the Tengyur (D4150), both of which share substantial textual alignments with the Pali text [Brough; DharmaNexus].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Resembling parallels (SuttaCentral): DN 31 (PTS DN iii 180) Siṅgāla Sutta; AN 4.19 Tatiyaagatisutta; an4.17-18
- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Catuttho bhāgo) (Atk S0513a4) (§5.3–13.4 ↔ §217–241); Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā (Atk S0512a) (§5.2–13.4 ↔ §991–1007); Catukkanipāta (AN 4) (§12.2–13.4 ↔ §19.3.2–19.4.4)
- Cross-language matches (DharmaNexus): སྐྱེས་པའི་རབས་ཀྱི་རྒྱུད། (jātakamāla) (D4150) [bo]; Āryaśūra: Jātakamālā (SA_T09_bsa032) [sa]
**Sources**

- [SuttaCentral] SuttaCentral entry for ja443 — Provided English title, frame story setting, and resemblance parallels to DN 31 and AN 4.17–19.
- [DharmaNexus] DharmaNexus text-reuse database — Supplied Pali reuse segments with Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā, Cariyāpiṭaka-aṭṭhakathā, and AN 4, as well as alignments with Āryaśūra's Jātakamālā and Tibetan D4150.
- [Morris 1882] Richard Morris (ed.), Cariyāpiṭaka (1882) — Attested placement in the Dasanipāta and relationship to the Cariyāpiṭaka verses.
- [Bareau] André Bareau, Les récits canoniques du Cariyāpiṭaka et les Jātaka Pāli — Documented the Cariyāpiṭaka account of Cūlabodhi renouncing alongside his brāhmaṇī wife to fulfill the perfection of virtue.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pali Language and Literature (1994) — Supplied narrative details regarding the king's abduction of Cūlabodhi's wife and the Bodhisatta's freedom from anger for sīlapāramī.
- [Anandajoti 2010] Bhikkhu Ānandajoti, Buddhist Wisdom Verses: 551 Verses from the Canon (2010) — Provided alternative title Cullabodhijātakam, narrative summary, and theme of destroying anger.
- [Brough] John Brough, The Chinese Pseudo-Translation of Ārya-Śūra's Jātaka-Mālā — Discussed Āryaśūra's Jātakamālā chapter 21 (Cuddabodhi) and its Tibetan translation corresponding to the Pali Jātaka.
- [War Yar Mein Da 2015] War Yar Mein Da, Paramis / Paramitas in Theravada and Mahayana (2015) — Noted the Bodhisatta's characterization as Cullaparibbājaka in Jātaka 443.
